correctness.rationale: For rank-one \(A=u\varphi\) and involutive \(U\), the nilpotent factor is uniquely \(N=AU\); rank-one nilpotence is exactly \(\operatorname{tr}(AU)=0\). The odd-characteristic involution/idempotent bijection \(U=I_3-2P\) and the characteristic-two square-zero parametrization \(U=I_3+S\) reduce the count to explicit projective incidence counts. Inclusion-exclusion and scaling-orbit factors were reconstructed separately. Exhaustive exact enumeration over \(\mathbb F_2\), \(\mathbb F_3\), and \(\mathbb F_4\) reproduces all specialized values.

General counts of all involutions solve \(U^2=I\) without the additional \(\operatorname{tr}(AU)=0\) constraint and therefore do not imply the claim.

value.rationale: The recent primary source explicitly flags non-uniqueness without quantifying it. The result gives a complete, field-uniform multiplicity classification on the natural rank-one stratum in the first dimension where the existence theory becomes nontrivial, and exposes a sharp characteristic-two versus odd-characteristic split. The invariant being counted—the size of the factorization fiber—is intrinsic to the decomposition problem rather than an arbitrary matrix slice.
